title: Louisiana family's bid to overturn 30-year-old inheritance ruling fails
description: A Louisiana man died without a will in 1956, and a court recognised his daughter as the heir to his estate in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, another family challenged her right to inherit a 50% share of a property. On October 30, the Louisiana Supreme Court rejected the challenge as legally time-barred, upholding the earlier inheritance ruling.

title: Alex Karp buys 37,000 acres of Swedish forest for $22M; why hunters are barred
description: Alex Karp acquired 15,000 hectares of forest land in Härjedalen, Sweden, through his company Cladonia Skog AB. The purchase was confirmed by Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget, which previously owned the forest land. Hunters in the area received notification about the termination of their leasing agreements after the sale. A representative from Cladonia expressed commitment to preserving the natural landscape and its habitats.

title: At 1,000 this fiscal, IndiGo set to hire most pilots in a year by an Indian carrier
description: IndiGo has made significant strides by onboarding 600 pilots in just the first half of this fiscal year. With plans to hire an additional 400 by March 2024, the airline is focused on compliance with pilot duty regulations and strategic international expansion. Given the current geopolitical climate, which is influencing operating costs like aviation turbine fuel, IndiGo is evaluating potential fuel hedging strategies to support its long-haul service growth.

title: US on right AI track; robots take jobs, right tax system needed: Larry Ellison
description: Larry Ellison emphasizes that AI advancements could lead to increased productivity and economic growth. He suggests that taxing the value generated by robots could replace traditional labor taxation methods. This approach could support a universal high income, improving living standards for individuals. Ellison believes that while some jobs may be displaced, automation will create opportunities for more efficient work.

title: Injecting to crush kilos: The rise of ‘Mounjaro’ brides
description: Increasingly, couples in India turn to prescription weight-loss medicines to enhance their appearance before weddings. Clinics in cities like Lucknow report a significant rise in inquiries about these medications. Many individuals seek rapid results to boost confidence for their special day, despite potential health risks. Medical professionals highlight the importance of eligibility criteria and caution against misuse of these drugs.

title: Delhi's vehicle ban faces its biggest test at borders: Can enforcement keep up?
description: Delhi is set to implement restrictions on older vehicles that fail to meet BS6 emission standards from entering the city. However, officials are grappling with the difficulty of monitoring numerous entry points, especially during rush hours. Leveraging technology, such as automatic number plate recognition, will be essential for identifying non-compliant vehicles. Collaboration between Delhi and neighboring NCR states is vital to prevent alternative routes and ensure effective enforcement.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s parenting choice kept their children away from tennis spotlight
description: Tennis legends Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi have two children, Jaden and Jaz, but neither followed their parents into professional tennis. Jaden pursued baseball, playing for USC and later representing Team Germany in World Baseball Classic Qualifiers. Jaz developed interests in dancing and horseback riding. The couple deliberately avoided putting sporting pressure on their children, choosing instead to let them discover their own passions and identities.
